ai.headline: Meta reports Q3 results as a New Mexico $25 billion penalty lands
ai.summary:
Interest in Meta stock is rising around two developments that landed on the same day. Meta was scheduled to release its third-quarter results after the market closed on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the first major report of Big Tech's earnings season. Analysts polled by Bloomberg expected earnings of about $3.56 per share and revenue near $63.3 billion, compared with $1.05 per share and $51.2 billion a year earlier. Capital spending was projected to rise roughly 117% to $41 billion, and Reality Labs was expected to post an operating loss of about $5.2 billion. Investors are watching closely because Meta is one of the largest AI spenders, and Bloomberg reported that a weak result could add to existing worries about the AI trade.

Separately, a New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in penalties, according to a court filing reported by CNBC. The case stems from the Cambridge Analytica scandal and a September jury finding that the company misled state residents about data privacy and the handling of harmful content. The jury counted more than 43 million violations under the state's unfair practices law, with a maximum of $5,000 each, but the judge set the final amount, which was reduced from a much larger figure the filing cited. The judge also said interest would accrue at 15% a year until the fine is paid. CNBC said it had contacted Meta for comment, and the company's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
key_points: Meta was set to report third-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday, October 21.
Bloomberg analyst consensus expected about $3.56 EPS and $63.3 billion in revenue, versus $1.05 and $51.2 billion a year earlier.
